lead: Portland's long rainy season, old houses and ice storms all lead to water damage. DryFlare helps homes from Sellwood to St. Johns get water out and dry properly.
risk: months of rain, basement water in older homes and ice-storm pipe bursts
risk_short: heavy rain, old basements, ice storms
why: The February 1996 flood brought the Willamette within inches of the top of the downtown seawall. Johnson Creek has flooded the Lents neighborhood many times. To cut sewer overflows, Portland built the "Big Pipe" tunnels, finished in 2011, but older homes still see basement backups in heavy rain.

More than a quarter of Portland homes were built before 1940. Old basements seep, foundations crack, and moss lifts shingles. In January 2024, an ice storm froze the city for days, bringing burst pipes and roof damage from fallen trees. Damp air keeps drying slow all winter.
image_alt: Flooded street with cars stranded under overgrown trees
image_caption: Heavy rain that floods Portland streets also pushes water into older basements.
problems: Older homes in Laurelhurst, Hawthorne, Alberta
Lents and areas near Johnson Creek
Homes with moss and tree damage
tips: Install a backwater valve if your basement has a floor drain.
Clean moss and gutters each fall.
Keep heat on and drip faucets during ice storms.
Have the sewer line scoped if you have big street trees.
areas: Calls come from the Pearl District, Sellwood, Hawthorne, Alberta Arts, St. Johns, Laurelhurst, Hillsdale and Lents, plus Beaverton, Gresham, Lake Oswego, Tigard and Milwaukie.

faq.a: It's a set of large sewer tunnels finished in 2011 to cut combined sewer overflows into the Willamette River and Columbia Slough. It reduced overflows, but heavy rain can still cause backups in older homes' drains.
